Marketing & Psychology.title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: A cult classic and national bestseller by Robert Cialdini, this book explores the key principles of persuasion—social proof, reciprocity, commitment, authority, liking, and scarcity—that are fundamental to marketing and sales. Backed by over 30 years of research, it reveals the psychological triggers that drive consumer behavior and how marketers can ethically leverage them to influence decisions.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Contagious: Why Things Catch On
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Wharton marketing professor Jonah Berger identifies six principles (STEPPS—Social Currency, Triggers, Emotion, Public, Practical Value, and Stories) that drive why certain ideas, products, and behaviors go viral. Blending cognitive psychology, sociology, and marketing, this book provides actionable techniques for making content more shareable and campaigns more influential.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman's landmark book distinguishes between two modes of thought: System 1 (fast, intuitive, emotional) and System 2 (slow, deliberate, logical). It reveals cognitive biases and heuristics that shape human decision-making, providing marketers with deep insights into how consumers truly process information and make choices—often irrationally.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Decoded: The Science Behind Why We Buy
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Phil Barden's groundbreaking book translates findings from neuroscience, behavioral economics, cognitive psychology, and decision science into practical marketing insights. It reveals the subconscious drivers behind consumer purchasing decisions, explaining why people buy what they buy and how marketers can connect with audiences on a deeper, more effective level.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Predictably Irrational
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Dan Ariely's bestselling exploration of the hidden forces that shape our decisions challenges the assumption of human rationality. Through engaging experiments and real-world examples, Ariely reveals how emotions, social norms, anchoring, and cognitive biases systematically influence consumer behavior—offering marketers a powerful framework for understanding and predicting customer choices.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Building a StoryBrand
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Donald Miller's bestselling guide uses the psychology of storytelling to help businesses clarify their message and connect with customers. By positioning the customer as the hero of the story and the brand as the guide, marketers can create compelling narratives that drive engagement, loyalty, and conversions. The seven-part StoryBrand framework is grounded in how the human brain naturally processes and remembers stories.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Purple Cow: Transform Your Business by Being Remarkable
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Seth Godin's influential book argues that traditional advertising is no longer effective in a cluttered world, and that the key to marketing success is creating remarkably different products that people can't ignore. Drawing on psychology and consumer behavior, Godin shows how standing out—being the "purple cow" in a field of ordinary ones—drives word-of-mouth and builds lasting brands.

Marketing & Psychology.title: Buyology: Truth and Lies About Why We Buy
Marketing & Psychology.abstract: Martin Lindstrom's groundbreaking neuromarketing study used brain-scanning technology on over 2,000 volunteers worldwide to uncover the subconscious forces that truly drive consumer decisions. The book reveals how emotions, branding, and unconscious triggers shape purchasing behavior—challenging conventional marketing wisdom with hard neuroscience evidence.
